name: Berobenatide
lead: Berobenatide (also written PF-08653944 and MET-097i) is an investigational long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist being developed by Pfizer for weight management. It is not approved anywhere and has no appearance-related indication. Information available publicly is limited to clinical trial registrations.[1][2]

Two Phase 3 trials are listed on ClinicalTrials.gov: one in adults with obstructive sleep apnea and overweight or obesity who use a PAP machine, which describes the drug as given monthly, and one in women with stress urinary incontinence and overweight or obesity.[1][2] No results from these trials have been published.

paras: Two Phase 3 trials are registered. VESPER-OSA 1 (NCT07823608) is recruiting about 258 adults with sleep-disordered breathing and overweight or obesity who use positive airway pressure, with a registered start of September 2026.[2] A second trial (NCT07932925) plans about 900 women with stress urinary incontinence and overweight or obesity and is listed as not yet recruiting.[1] No published efficacy or safety results were found.
No community discussion of berobenatide in looksmaxxing forums was found. Its relevance to the wiki is as a pipeline member of the GLP-1 class used for fat loss.

card.summary: Pfizer's investigational monthly GLP-1 agonist for obesity; only Phase 3 registrations exist so far.
card.note: Unapproved investigational drug; no published results.

quick.overview:
Berobenatide is an experimental GLP-1 receptor agonist from Pfizer, aimed at weight management. It is not approved for any use.

The public record consists of two Phase 3 trial registrations, in sleep apnea and in stress urinary incontinence, each in people with overweight or obesity. No results have been published.
quick.mechanism: As a GLP-1 receptor agonist it is expected to act like other drugs in the class, which reduce appetite and slow gastric emptying. The registry describes monthly dosing.
quick.risks: Safety in humans has not been published. It is an unapproved investigational drug and not available through legitimate prescribing.
